items.prompt: Why can Python print False for 0.1+0.2==0.3?
items.explanation: Many decimal fractions have only approximate binary floating-point representations. The equality compares the resulting stored values; this is not random arithmetic.

options.text: The decimal literals become approximate binary floats
options.why: Their representations can differ after addition, so exact equality can fail.

options.text: Python randomly chooses a final decimal rounding direction
options.why: This calculation is deterministic; random selection is not the cause.

options.text: Python treats all three literals as whole-number integers
options.why: The decimal point makes these float literals, not integer literals.

options.text: Equality is evaluated before the addition on the left
options.why: Addition binds more tightly; the stored results are compared.
